description: This course covers the main developments and themes in Europe from the fourteenth to seventeenth
centuries, drawing on some of the on-going debates about the period, and giving particular
attention to the powerful but often unpredictable influences of ideas and economic change in
shaping institutions and people's experiences, including the Renaissance, literary and Christian
humanism, the Protestant and Catholic Reformations, the rise of state power, merchant capitalism,
European expansion, and the Scientific Revolution. Offered annually during fall semester.
